document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What do I set up before running production from the new BOM?
content: Four things are defined first: the Operation Library, the Operation Time Component, the Operation Cost Template and the Operation Parameter. Together they say which production processes exist, how long they take, what they cost and how efficient they are.
steps:
1. Operation Library: add the production processes, then define operations and sub-operations (and machine sub-categories if required).
2. Operation Time Component: add time components such as production time, queue time and preparation time.
3. Operation Cost Template: add operation costs such as production charges, overhead and dyeing charges, with their cost components.
4. Operation Parameter: define efficiency and loss % against the production process, operation and sub-operation.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What is the Operation Library?
content: The Operation Library holds the production processes with their operations and sub-operations and, if required, machine sub-categories. Development is under way so that production can later be tracked sub-operation wise.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What is the Operation Time Component?
content: It lets you add time components to an operation: production time, queue time and preparation time.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What is the Operation Cost Template?
content: It lets you add operation costs such as production charges, overhead and dyeing charges, each with its cost components.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What is the Operation Parameter?
content: Against a production process, operation and sub-operation you define efficiency and loss %. You can also define the total quantity produced with respect to the total time, including production time, queue time and others where applicable.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: How is recipe management set up?
content: Recipes describe a dyeing or wet process. You create a recipe group, a recipe category, optionally a light master, and then the recipe itself.
steps:
1. Recipe Group: create it for the categories and product group sub-categories (Production > Recipe > Recipe Group).
2. Recipe Category: create it so that recipes can be created (Production > Recipe > Recipe Category).
3. Light Master (optional): shows which type of light is used in the process (Production > Recipe > Light Master).
4. Recipe: create it by adding the total water consumption and the liquid consumption.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What are the recipe types Batch and Continuous?
content: Batch is used to send the fabric in one bunch. Continuous is used to send the fabric one by one.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What is Pickup % in a recipe?
content: In the dyeing process, pickup is the percentage of dye that is absorbed by the fabric.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: What are BOM views and how are they given to users?
content: The new BOM can have several views per user group. In a view you can make fields visible or editable, pin them to the left or right and widen them. The View Configuration screen creates the view templates and assigns permissions.
notes: Views are given to users from Program Permission. A user can be given several views.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: How do I create a new BOM?
content: Create the new BOM using a template and define all the fabric and trim articles in it.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: How do I make a fabric that is produced by a process such as dyeing?
content: Mark the fabric as Manufacturing and attach a Manufacturing BOM to it. After the total BOM cost is approved, the cost of the processed fabric updates automatically in the Style BOM once the fabric BOM is attached to it.
steps:
1. Mark the fabric article as Manufacturing.
2. Add a new BOM under the fabric article.
3. Define the articles that are to be processed to produce the main fabric article.
4. Add a recipe if one is required.
5. Approve the total BOM cost; the fabric cost then flows into the Style BOM.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: How do I run MRP with the new BOM and a manufacturing fabric?
content: Link the buyer order with the actual order quantity and attach the orders, run MRP, and mark the order quantity as Mark for Purchase or Mark for Production. A second level of MRP generates the recipe articles when a recipe is attached at the second level.
steps:
1. Link the buyer order with the actual order quantity and attach the orders.
2. Run MRP and mark the order quantity as Mark for Purchase or Mark for Production.
3. Run the second level of MRP to generate the recipe articles, if a recipe is attached at the second level.
4. Two production orders are created because the fabric has a manufacturing BOM: one against the style and one against the fabric article.
5. A PD is also created at material requirement planning, because processes are defined in Material Linkage in both the fabric BOM and the style BOM.
6. Define the FPO and FPPOs for both the manufacturing BOM (process order) and the production orders and proceed.
notes: If the required quantity does not come against the recipe article, check that a conversion is defined between the Sample Weight UOM and the article UOM on the recipe.

document: New BOM, Recipe Management and MRP SOP
title: Can I add a recipe when creating the FPPO?
content: Yes. The recipe can be added at the time of FPPO creation. The articles in the recipe are added to the FPPO, appear in the dispatch instruction list, and an indent is added in the adhoc indent details on the FPPO page.

title: How do I start AI tech pack mapping for the Classic team?
content: AI tech pack mapping needs a package per buyer, a package mapping, a one-time mapping on the AI screen and then the PDF upload.
steps:
1. Ask the tech team to create a new package per buyer; the tech team creates four packages.
2. Do the package configuration on the package configuration screen.
3. Do the package mapping for all the packages.
4. Do the one-time mapping (OTM) on the AI screen with the uploaded PDF and confirm the setup.
5. Upload the tech pack PDF.

title: What is configured in the AI tech pack package?
content: In the package configuration you can give a generic article, which is added in the Auto BOM when the BOM is created. The generic fabric and trim articles must be created before the package configuration so that they can be tagged to the package. Article and purchase officer configuration helps add the article in the BOM, and the article request is assigned to the user who is responsible for confirming the material.

title: What does the package mapping do and can I correct what AI picks?
content: The user does the package mapping for all the packages. The mapping has an Editable option, so the user can fill the data manually if the AI does not pick it correctly.

title: What is the one-time mapping (OTM) for an AI tech pack and what are the PDF limits?
content: On the AI screen the user selects the tech pack and does the OTM with the uploaded PDF, then confirms the setup.
notes: The PDF can be at most 10 MB and at most 50 pages, as per the current structure. The upload status is shown on a line on the screen and takes about 3 to 4 minutes depending on the PDF size.
